ety.text: Inherited from Old Hindi चैंन (caiṃna). Cognate with Gujarati ચેન (cen), Marathi चैन (cain), Nepali चैन् (caina), Odia ଚଇନ (caina), and Sindhi چَيْنُ (cainu). Further origin is uncertain. Perhaps related to Prakrit चइअ (caïa, “possible”), चायंत (cāyaṃta, “enabling”), चाइय (cāiya, “made able”), related to Sanskrit चकति (cakati, “is satisfied”). Or, from Sanskrit शयन (śáyana); for the shift in initial consonant, compare Ashokan Prakrit 𑀘𑀖𑀢𑀺 (caghati, “is able”) < Sanskrit शक्ष्यति (śakṣyati).
Inherited from Sanskrit क्षण (kṣaṇa). Doublet of क्षण (kṣaṇ).

Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀝𑁆𑀞𑀸𑀯𑁂𑀇 (paṭṭhāvei) or Prakrit 𑀧𑀝𑁆𑀞𑀯ï (paṭṭhavaï), from Sanskrit प्रस्थापयति (prasthāpayati). Cognate to Awadhi पठवब (paṭhvab), Bhojpuri 𑂣𑂘𑂰𑂫𑂪 (paṭhāval), Gujarati પઠાવવું (paṭhāvvũ), Punjabi ਪਥਾਉਣਾ (pathāuṇā), Nepali पठाउनु (paṭhāunu).

ety.text: Alteration of Prakrit 𑀨𑁂𑀧𑁆𑀨𑀲 n (phĕpphasa) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀟- (-ḍa-) + -𑀓- (-ka-), from a variety of onomatopoeic words for "lung" from the sound of blowing or puffing, ultimately related to Sanskrit फुफुस m (phuphusa, “lung”). Cognate to Gujarati ફેફસું (phephsũ) and Sindhi फिफड़. Related to फप्फस (phapphas), फफसा (phaphsā, “swollen”). Doublet of फुप्फुस (phupphus), a tatsama.
